analysis: The PR change in the supplied file_changes is a single added documentation table row at docs/architecture/inference.md head line 1406 (`demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens`, paged complete store floor for dense Qwen3.5/3.8, referencing EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift). The two supplied units (head lines 1-805) are unchanged surrounding documentation. I read them for security-relevant statements. They cover Nemotron Super prefix-cache behavior (cache scope partitioning by authenticated tenant, durable SSD checkpoints encrypted under the provider cache root, no scope means cold and no publish), the TB-007 inference engine, and the T-041 prefix-cache posture. Nothing in the supplied text loosens the T-041 controls. Cache scope remains coordinator-authored, there is no TTL change, and no on-disk metadata change. The new row describes a checkpoint-placement heuristic (a range ends just below the prompt end when it saves at least the floor). It is described as an effective-token floor on checkpoint creation and not as a change to naming, AAD, TTL, scope or encryption. No code is supplied, so I could not verify that the implementation in EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift preserves salt/scope folding in HMAC lookup tags or the per-donation adoption/benefit gating. Whether an end-of-prompt checkpoint could widen the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035, accepted risk) or the at-rest surface for dense Qwen3.5/3.8 is not established here. The next pass should check that source if available. The doc-only change introduces no regression I can evidence, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated by the visible text.
